{"type":"text","timestamp":1794659933780,"sessionID":"ses_e25f29c89ffe1mLIsTDCbpx4L8","part":{"id":"prt_1da115e4b001tVHolnqHYD7a5a","messageID":"msg_1da11453c001tp7quHABfHM8qb","sessionID":"ses_e25f29c89ffe1mLIsTDCbpx4L8","type":"text","text":"I've submitted \"Origami Fleet\", a 14-instruction warrior of my own. Against the 30 sparring warriors it averaged about 0.35 points per round (200 rounds each), where 1.0 means winning every round. I couldn't test it against the hidden hill, so I don't know its actual reward.\n\n**How it works:** it's a three-stage silk paper (a replicator). It starts by splitting into 16 processes. Each copy then copies itself to three new places in the core. Along the way it drops `dat <2667, <5334` bombs, which are aimed at damaging imps.\n\n**What I tried before settling on it** (sparring averages, 100–200 rounds each):\n\n| version | score |\n|---|---|\n| final paper, 16 processes | 0.349–0.353 |\n| same paper with 8 or 32 processes | 0.31 |\n| 0.5c scanner followed by a core clear | about 0.31 |\n| p-space switcher between the paper and the scanner | 0.33–0.34 |\n| stone (bomber) with a 3-point imp ring | 0.26 |\n\nChanging the paper's copy distances, bomb type or loop constant gave 0.31–0.35. All of that is within noise, so I kept the original numbers.\n\n**Weaknesses:** it ties a lot and still loses most rounds against roughly a third of the sparring warriors. The scanner I added through the p-space switch didn't help, because the scanner itself was weak. A quick-scan opening or a properly tuned scanner partner would be the next things to try.\n\nThe source is at `/tmp/w/pr.red` and it is the current submission on the server.","time":{"start":1794659933771,"end":1794659933778}}}
